How much does it cost to charge an electric toothbrush?

Charging an electric toothbrush typically draws about 2 watts (1–5W depending on the model). Used for 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, it costs about 1.3p per day and £4.60 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per day
1.3p
About £4.60 a year at 24 hours per day, 7 days a week.

Standing charge not included.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Most of these cost pennies; the bigger users are anything that heats, like hair dryers.
  • Unplug chargers once devices are full.
  • Use a lower heat setting where it does the job.

Questions

How much does it cost to charge an electric toothbrush per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 2W model costs about 0.1p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to charge an electric toothbrush per year?

About £4.60 a year, based on 24 hours per day, 7 days a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my electric toothbrush's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
